title: Slow androgenetic hair loss and produce regrowth with approved medicines

concept.text: Modify common pattern hair loss pharmacologically, increasing or maintaining visible scalp hair during treatment. Finasteride and topical minoxidil established this capability; they do not create a new supply of follicles. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for androgenetic alopecia supported by controlled human trials showing improved target-area hair counts and photographic or patient assessments over approximately one year. Test set by: FDA; Propecia's pivotal programme used hair counts, standardized photographs and patient/investigator assessments. Reported achieved: FDA approved finasteride 1 mg (Propecia) for male pattern hair loss on 19 December 1997; topical minoxidil was already an established treatment. Sources given: [FDA confirmation of Propecia approval date](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/human-drug-compounding/fda-alerts-health-care-providers-compounders-and-consumers-potential-risks-associated-compounded) ; [Propecia clinical evidence and prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=9e7329eb-39f1-4f84-a0bb-91daffaba1c3&type=display) ; [Topical minoxidil women's hair-regrowth label](https://dailymed.awsprod.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=c3ba93d7-e826-f6ac-e053-2a95a90a7951).

page.title: Pharmacological treatment of androgenetic alopecia
page.definition: Approved medicines slow androgenetic alopecia, the progressive loss of scalp hair in a characteristic pattern, and produce regrowth during treatment. Topical minoxidil and oral finasteride establish this capability in their approved populations; continued treatment is needed to retain benefit.

goal.need: A 2001 clinic study examined 377 women aged 18–99 years for female pattern hair loss; its age-specific frequencies appear below. Progression is measurable in men: in two finasteride studies enrolling 1,553 men, 58% of placebo recipients had further target-area hair loss at 12 months.

figures.caption: Female pattern hair loss in a dermatology-clinic sample
columns: Diagnosed with female pattern hair loss
figures.note: The 377 women attended for complaints unrelated to hair growth. These are clinic-sample frequencies, not population prevalence estimates.

statements.quote: Patients are looking for effective hair loss treatments to prevent further thinning and optimally stimulate regrowth.
Treatment can prevent hair loss from worsening and help women regrow their hair.
statements.context: The passage concerns female pattern hair loss.

completion.title: FDA approves a medicine specifically for androgenetic alopecia in the relevant population.
completion.criterion: FDA issues final marketing approval for a medicine specifically to treat androgenetic alopecia in the relevant population. Its evidence and labeling establish hair regrowth or prevention of further pattern hair loss, and it meets statutory requirements for safety, effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling. The approval decision is the threshold; the regulation leaves the kind and quantity of supporting evidence to FDA's scientific judgment.
completion.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 314.105(c), applied through indication-specific marketing approval.
completion.threshold_quote: FDA will approve an NDA after it determines that the drug meets the statutory standards for safety and effectiveness
completion.basis: Achieved. FDA records Rogaine's original approval on 17 August 1988 and Propecia's approval on 19 December 1997. Approved topical minoxidil also exists for women. Propecia's indication is restricted to men. Both medicines require continued treatment to retain benefit. Approval provides an externally determined test tied to a defined medicine, indication and population.

milestones.title: Nonclinical evidence supports reasonably safe human testing of a candidate hair-loss medicine.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology establish that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe; required tests depend on its nature and duration. Laboratory evidence relevant to both clinical populations includes a 1987 study of 18 stump-tailed macaques: topical minoxidil 2% and 5% enlarged small follicles into intermediate or terminal follicles producing larger hairs. This is pharmacology evidence; satisfaction of the complete toxicology requirement cannot be established from that paper alone.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), the pharmacology and toxicology requirement for an investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: A candidate hair-loss medicine reaches human administration in clinical research.
milestones.criterion: A candidate medicine is administered to people in monitored clinical research. A 1985 study gave nine scalp applications of 1% or 5% minoxidil to 12 adult men; urinary recovery was 1.6–3.9% of the applied dose, and no adverse reactions were observed. A study published in 1988 tested the efficacy and safety of 3% topical minoxidil in 25 women. These document human exposure without establishing that either publication describes the first exposure in its population.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, initial human testing under Phase I Clinical Studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: Controlled studies provide preliminary evidence that a medicine treats pattern hair loss.
milestones.criterion: Controlled studies provide preliminary evidence of effectiveness and characterize short-term risks. In a 1985 minoxidil study, 126 men completed 12 months; 2% and 3% solutions increased terminal hair growth versus placebo at 4 months, before placebo crossover. In a 1991 study, 28 women received 2% minoxidil or vehicle twice daily for 32 weeks; counts excluding fine vellus hairs favored minoxidil (p=0.006), but patients perceived no between-group difference.
milestones.set_by: FDA, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c), controlled efficacy studies and the prerequisite for expanded clinical trials.
milestones.threshold_quote: preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

milestones.title: Expanded trials establish a medicine's benefit–risk profile for treating pattern hair loss.
milestones.criterion: Expanded trials provide effectiveness and safety evidence sufficient for benefit–risk evaluation and prescribing information. Men: two 12-month finasteride 1 mg/day studies enrolled 1,553; the 12-month difference was 107 hairs per 5.1 cm² versus placebo (p<0.001; 679 treated and 672 placebo recipients assessed). Women: a 32-week trial of 2% topical minoxidil enrolled 308, with 256 completing; mean increases were 23 versus 11 nonvellus hairs/cm² with placebo (95% confidence interval for the difference, 5.9–17.5). No serious or unexpected medical events were reported in the women's trial.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase 3 Clinical Studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship of the drug.

not_found: No FDA or society document located specified a universal minimum hair-count gain or a mandatory one-year trial for androgenetic alopecia medicines.
The original minoxidil hair-loss IND clearance and its complete supporting toxicology package were not located.

results.finding: Rat fertility studies (sample size not stated): oral minoxidil doses of at least 3 mg/kg/day were associated with reduced fertility measures.
results.detail: The product label also summarizes safety pharmacology, repeated-dose toxicity, genotoxicity and carcinogenicity studies. It does not report nonclinical evidence of minoxidil's hair-growth activity or establish the complete requirements for a specified human investigation.
results.quote: Preclinical fertility studies in rats have shown minoxidil doses equal or greater than 3 mg/kg/day (at least 8 fold human exposure) when administered orally and greater than 9 mg/kg (at least 25-fold human exposure) administered subcutaneously in rats were associated with reduced conception and implantation rates as well as reduction in the number of live pups.

results.finding: In 25 women with androgenetic alopecia, researchers studied 3% topical minoxidil.
results.quote: To investigate the usefulness of topical minoxidil therapy in female androgenetic alopecia, we studied the efficacy and safety of 3% topical minoxidil in 25 affected women.

results.finding: In 126 men with early male pattern baldness, topical minoxidil significantly increased terminal hair growth versus placebo at 4 months.
results.detail: The randomized, double-blind study provides preliminary evidence of effectiveness, but the supplied text does not characterize short-term risks.
results.quote: Treatment of subjects with topical minoxidil for 4 months resulted in a statistically significant increase in terminal hair growth in comparison with placebo therapy.

results.finding: In 28 women with androgenetic alopecia, nonvellus hair counts favored 2% minoxidil over vehicle at 32 weeks (p = 0.006).
results.detail: Women applied minoxidil or vehicle twice daily. Participants perceived no difference between groups, and the provided text does not characterize short-term risks.
results.quote: At the end of thirty-two weeks, there was a statistically significant increase of nonvellus target area hairs in the minoxidil-treated versus the vehicle-treated group (p = 0.006).

results.finding: In 113 women with androgenetic alopecia, 5% minoxidil foam increased target-area hair count by 16.2% at 24 weeks.
results.detail: The randomized study found the foam noninferior to 2% minoxidil solution and assessed short-term adverse effects. It had no placebo arm; participants were not blinded.
results.quote:
At the end of the study, TAHC and
TAHW increased by 16.2% and 19.6%, respectively,
in women randomized to 5% MTF compared with an
increase of 13.8% and 17.8%, respectively, in women
randomized to 2% MTS.

results.finding: In two trials enrolling 1,553 men, finasteride increased hair count by 107 hairs per 5.1 cm² versus placebo at 12 months.
results.detail: The trials also reported safety outcomes: sexual-function adverse events occurred in 4.2% of finasteride recipients versus 2.2% of placebo recipients in the first year.
results.quote:
Clinically significant increases in hair count
(baseline = 876 hairs), measured in a 1-inch diameter circular area (5.1 cm 2) of balding
vertex scalp, were observed with finasteride treatment (107 and 138 hairs vs placebo at 1
and 2 years, respectively; P < .001).

results.finding: Finasteride in 1,553 men with male pattern hair loss: durable hair improvements over five years.
results.detail: Two 1-year trials were followed by placebo-controlled extensions involving 1,215 men. The source reports efficacy and tolerability but does not provide the criterion's 12-month hair-count difference or assessed sample sizes.
results.quote: Treatment with finasteride led to durable improvements in scalp hair over five years (p 3/4 0.001 versus placebo, all endpoints), while treatment with placebo led to progressive hair loss. Finasteride was generally well tolerated and no new safety concerns were identified during long-term use.

results.finding: Female pattern hair loss: 381 women enrolled; 2% minoxidil increased hair count by 20.7 versus 9.4 hairs/cm² with placebo at 48 weeks.
results.detail: This 48-week trial provides effectiveness and safety evidence, but it is not the specified 32-week trial of 308 women. Approximately 30% of participants dropped out; efficacy was assessed in an evaluable population.

results.finding: In 397 women with female pattern hair loss, 5% minoxidil foam increased hair count by 9.1 hairs/cm² more than vehicle at 24 weeks.
results.detail: The prescribing information reports phase 3 efficacy and safety evidence, but not the specified 32-week trial of 2% minoxidil in 308 women or its results.
results.quote:
After 24 weeks of treatment, the 5% MTF OD group re-grew 13.4 hairs/cm
2
and the foam vehicle group re-grew 4.3 hairs/cm
2
, a treatment difference of 9.1 hairs/cm
2
(p<0.0001).

results.finding: FDA approved 5% minoxidil topical aerosol for female pattern hair loss; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The approval covers nonprescription treatment of female pattern hair loss on the top of the scalp.
results.quote:
This sNDA provides for the use of Women’s Rogaine (5% minoxidil) Topical Aerosol for the 
nonprescription treatment of female pattern hair loss/androgenetic alopecia on the top of the 
scalp. 
We have completed our review of this application, as amended.  It is approved, effective on the 
date of this letter
